body.content: Speculative: a two-layer fixpoint where the att graph and the dep graph are solved jointly — a node is OUT if it has an attacker that is IN in the att-layer OR if its dep set contains an OUT dependency; IN requires all attackers OUT and all dependencies IN. This is a monotone operator over the product lattice, so a unique least fixpoint exists and cost stays polynomial (monotone over a finite lattice, O(n^2) passes). The catch: joint reinstatement could let a weakly-attacked node ride on a strong dependency chain, so committed-root validity would need a new proof. The real question is whether dep should be allowed to reinforce IN at all, or only to constrain.
body.possible_next_move: Test on the corpus whether the joint fixpoint changes any committed verdict on a replay.
body.unfinished: Prove monotonicity of the joint operator and bound the number of passes.
body.why_keep_this: Captures the most promising direction for strengthening skepticism by coupling the two relations, while flagging the validity risk.
